title: Jebel Faya, Sharjah
summary: Jebel Faya, a rock shelter in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, holds stone tools from about 127,000 to 123,000 years ago. A 2011 Science study dated a toolkit there to roughly 125,000 years ago and compared it with East African industries, arguing that people reached Arabia far earlier than the older 60,000-year model.

uncertainty.note: Assemblage C dated about 127–123 ka at Royal Holloway; the 2011 press summary gives 100,000 to 125,000 years. Years before present, not calibrated to 1950.

where.modern_name: Jebel Faya (Jabal Al Fayah), Emirate of Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
where.historical_name: Jebel Faya, southeastern Arabia; no polity

importance.justification: Central site in the debate over an early dispersal of modern humans into Arabia.

sources.title: Humans migrated out of Africa earlier than thought (Science, 2011)
The environmental context of Paleolithic settlement at Jebel Faya, Emirate Sharjah, UAE

reviewer_note: Identity of the toolmakers is unresolved (no human bones), so the record claims tools, not fossils; the link to Homo sapiens is contested. Dates differ between the 2011 press summary and the later university abstract. The Science paper itself was not opened.
